media.title: selective attention test (Simons & Chabris 1999 original stimulus video)

timecodes.what: White-on-black instruction card: 'This is a test of selective attention. Count how many times the players wearing white pass the basketball.'

William James Hall 14th-floor elevator bay: three brushed-steel double elevator doors in back, black 'S' curves taped on the two cream wall pillars between the doors. Three players in white t-shirts and three players in black t-shirts weave in tight figure-eights passing two orange basketballs (bounce passes and aerial chest passes).

At 00:25, Elisa Cheng in a full dark brown-black shaggy gorilla suit enters from the right edge in front of the rightmost elevator door, walks between the weaving players to dead center in front of the middle elevator door (00:28-00:30), turns squarely toward the camera, raises both furry fists and thumps her chest three times, then turns left and walks out the left edge at 00:34 (9 seconds total on screen).
The six players continue weaving and passing the two basketballs until the 15th White-team pass completes.
Black title cards: 'How many passes did you count?', 'The correct answer is 15 passes.', 'But did you see the gorilla?!'

shot_notes: Camera is a single fixed eye-level wide shot framing a 3 m deep by 5.2 m wide elevator lobby from knee/ankles to just above the three elevator door frames.

Background geometry: three brushed-steel double elevator doors evenly spaced across a pale cream wall, with white rectangular floor-indicator plaques above each door and black 'S' target curves taped on the wall piers between the left/center and center/right doors.

Cast wardrobe contrast: White team wears plain loose white t-shirts and blue/light denim jeans; Black team wears plain black t-shirts and black/dark trousers; Gorilla wears a full-body shaggy dark brown-black fur suit.

Action choreography: Both teams stay in constant overlapping motion across the same central floor zone so the viewer must actively track white shirts and suppress black shirts; the gorilla enters right-to-left at the exact same depth plane as the players, pauses dead center in front of the middle elevator door, faces the lens squarely, pounds its chest with both fists, and exits left without any player glancing at it.

media.title: The Monkey Business Illusion (Simons 2010 follow-up video)

timecodes.what: Title and instruction card: 'Count how many times the players wearing white pass the ball.'

Six players (3 white shirts, 3 black shirts) pass two basketballs (16 passes) in front of a pleated stage curtain. While the gorilla enters from right to left and thumps its chest at center frame, the backdrop curtain gradually shifts colour from bright crimson red to warm gold, and one black-shirted player backs out of the frame on the left.
Reveal cards and full rewind showing that viewers who knew to look for the gorilla spotted it but missed both the curtain colour change and the departing player.

media.license_note: Copyright 2010 Daniel J. Simons. Analyzed locally via keyframes and contact sheet (media/M2_monkey_business_illusion/) for blocking and prop changes only; never reused in channel videos.

shot_notes: Demonstrates visually how expecting one specific surprise (the gorilla) still leaves the observer blind to two other simultaneous large changes in the same frame (curtain colour shift from red to gold, and a player walking offstage).
